title: Useful math Tools
goal: In this lesson you will learn handy tools: abs, round, min, max, and math.ceil / math.floor.
learn: Use abs, round, min, and max
idea: Python has built-in helpers that do not need import: abs() (absolute value), round(), min(), and max(). From the math module: math.ceil(x) rounds up to the next whole number. math.floor(x) rounds down. These tools clean up messy numbers when you need whole counts or the biggest/smallest value.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change round(3.7) to round(3.2). Press Run. That line should print 3.

practice.text: Print the absolute value of -42 using abs().
practice.hint: abs() drops the minus sign and keeps the distance from zero. Put -42 inside abs().
practice.starterTip: Fill the print line with abs(-42). The output should be 42, not -42.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if abs(-42) is used and output is 42.

practice.text: Import math. Print math.ceil(7.2) and math.floor(7.2) on two lines.
practice.hint: ceil rounds up to the next whole number; floor rounds down. Same number, two different answers.
practice.starterTip: First print(math.ceil(7.2)) for 8, then print(math.floor(7.2)) for 7 on the next line.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if outputs are 8 and 7 using ceil and floor.

quiz.question: What does abs(-5) return?
quiz.correct: abs removes the minus sign: distance from zero.

quiz.question: What does math.ceil(2.1) return?
quiz.correct: ceil rounds up to the next whole number.

quiz.question: What does max(3, 10, 7) return?
quiz.wrong: max means the biggest number in the group.
